description: Challenge C2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Squalid has /ɑ/ in its first syllable. Squint has /ɪ/, squelch has /ɛ/, and squirm has /ɜr/.
Quixotic begins with /kwɪ/. Quiescent begins with /kwiː/, quench with /kwɛ/, and quorum with /kwɔ/.
Vexation begins with /vɛ/. Vacation begins with /veɪ/, vocation with /voʊ/, and vivacious with /vɪ/.
Gnomic begins with /n/ because its written g is silent. Comic begins with /k/, gibberish with /dʒ/, and homing with /h/.
Rhinoceros begins with /r/; h in rh is silent. Linoleum begins with /l/, hilarious with /h/, and villainous with /v/.
Xenial begins with /z/, although it is written with x. Sarcasm begins with /s/, charisma with /k/, and harbor with /h/.
Thrusts ends with the /sts/ cluster. Thrust and trussed end with /st/, while thrusting has a different final syllable.
Strengths ends with /ŋθs/. Strength ends with /ŋθ/, strengthen adds a syllable, and strenuous has a different ending.
Crunched ends with /tʃt/. Crunch ends with /tʃ/, crunches with /ɪz/, and crunching with /ɪŋ/.
Bourgeois is pronounced /ˌbʊrˈʒwɑ/ in General American, with an irregular French-derived spelling. The alternatives have distinct vowel and consonant sequences.
Phlegmatic is pronounced /flɛɡˈmætɪk/, with ph representing /f/. The alternatives begin with different consonants and have distinct first-syllable sounds.
Indictment is pronounced /ɪnˈdaɪtmənt/; c is silent. The alternatives have different stressed vowels and consonant sequences.
